steps.name: Normalize counts and filter low-expression genes
steps.question: How should the raw Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 12 samples) be normalized so that per-sample gene set scoring (GSVA) operates on a comparable continuous expression scale, given one sample (sample_01) has a library size ~4x below the median?
acceptance_criteria: Counts matrix and metadata are loaded and sample/gene dimensions confirmed (12 samples, ~12000 genes)
Low-count genes are filtered (e.g. edgeR filterByExpr or a CPM-based rule) before normalization
A variance-stabilized or log2-CPM normalized expression matrix is produced (e.g. via DESeq2 vst/rlog or edgeR voom/logCPM)
Library size of sample_01 relative to the cohort is reported explicitly and the sample is retained but flagged, not silently dropped
Output normalized matrix (genes x samples, gene symbols as rownames) is saved for downstream GSVA scoring

steps.name: GSVA hallmark pathway activity scoring per sample
steps.context: Uses the normalized expression matrix from T1S1 and the MSigDB human Hallmark gene sets (50 sets, HGNC symbols) available in the reference store at /mnt/refs/managed/msigdb-hallmark-human/2026.1/. Gene identifiers in the counts matrix must be confirmed/mapped to HGNC symbols (using the human UniProt ID mapping reference if the counts are keyed by Ensembl/Entrez IDs) before running GSVA, since gene set membership is symbol-based.
steps.question: What is the single-sample GSVA activity score for each of the 50 MSigDB Hallmark gene sets, for each of the 12 colon samples (6 UC-inflamed, 6 control)?
acceptance_criteria: Gene identifiers in the expression matrix are confirmed as (or mapped to) HGNC symbols matching the Hallmark GMT gene symbols; report the mapping rate
GSVA is run with the Hallmark gene set collection producing a samples x 50-pathway score matrix covering all 12 samples
Output score matrix is saved as a CSV with one row per sample and one column per hallmark pathway
Report the fraction of hallmark gene sets that had adequate gene coverage in this 12000-gene count matrix (sets with too few genes present should be flagged, not silently included)

steps.name: Differential hallmark pathway activity: UC-inflamed vs control
steps.context: Uses the GSVA score matrix from T1S2 and the metadata condition labels. Unpaired two-group design, single batch, n=6 vs 6 — an unpaired t-test or Wilcoxon rank-sum test per pathway with multiple-testing correction (Benjamini-Hochberg) is appropriate at this sample size; do not attempt a complex model given n=12 total.
steps.question: Which of the 50 hallmark pathway activity scores differ significantly between UC-inflamed (n=6) and control (n=6) colon samples?
acceptance_criteria: Per-pathway unpaired test (t-test or Wilcoxon) comparing UC-inflamed vs control computed for all 50 hallmark scores
BH-adjusted p-values reported alongside raw p-values and effect size (mean difference or rank-biserial)
A ranked table of pathways by adjusted p-value / effect size is produced
Sensitivity check: results are reported with and without sample_01 (the low-library-size outlier) to confirm no single sample drives a top hit

steps.name: Heatmap of hallmark pathway activity across samples
steps.context: Uses the GSVA score matrix (T1S2) and the differential test results (T1S3) to build a clustered, annotated heatmap: rows = 50 hallmark pathways (or the subset with adequate coverage), columns = 12 samples, annotated by condition (UC-inflamed vs control) and flagging sample_01 as a low-library-size outlier in the column annotation.
steps.question: What does the sample x hallmark-pathway activity landscape look like, and which pathways visually separate UC-inflamed from control colon samples?
acceptance_criteria: Heatmap renders all samples (12 columns) and all scored hallmark pathways (rows), scores z-scored per pathway across samples for visualization
Column annotation bar marks condition (UC-inflamed vs control) and flags sample_01 as a QC outlier
Pathways significant at BH-adjusted p<0.05 from T1S3 are highlighted/ordered separately or marked in a side annotation
Both row and column hierarchical clustering are shown (or explicitly justified if suppressed)
Output saved as a static image file (PNG/PDF) plus the underlying scored matrix as CSV

plan.title: GSVA hallmark pathway activity scoring in UC colon
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is bulk RNA-seq gene-level counts from Salmon (12000 genes x 12 samples: 6 UC-inflamed vs 6 control colon, unpaired, single batch) with one low-library-size outlier (sample_01, ~4x below median). To get a per-sample pathway activity score suitable for a heatmap, raw counts must first be normalized to a variance-stabilized/log scale (counts are not usable directly for single-sample gene set scoring, which assumes a continuous, roughly comparable expression scale across genes and samples). GSVA is the appropriate method here because it produces one continuous enrichment score per sample per gene set (unlike GSEA, which needs a ranked list per comparison, not per sample), which directly answers 'a pathway activity score for every sample'. The 50 MSigDB Hallmark human gene sets (present in the reference store, matching the human/colon data) are the natural gene-set collection for a first-pass 'which pathways separate treated from control' view. After scoring, the plan differentially tests each hallmark score between UC-inflamed and control with a simple two-group test (paired to the small n=6/6 unpaired design) and renders the full sample x pathway score matrix as an annotated heatmap, flagging the differential ones, so the user sees both individual sample scores and group separation. The outlier sample is flagged throughout rather than silently dropped, since removing it would leave an unbalanced 5v6 design.
